strings.page.title: GitHub Desktop for Linux: package repository
strings.header.title: GitHub Desktop for Linux
strings.header.intro: Package repository for the maintained Linux builds. Add it once, then upgrade with the rest of your system.
strings.channels.heading: Choose a channel
strings.channels.intro: Pick one. Your package manager then keeps you on the newest version of that channel by itself, with no download to repeat.
strings.channels.stable.name: Stable
strings.channels.stable.serves: A version that has been in use for a while without a known issue. Promoted by hand, never on the day it is released.
strings.channels.stable.chooseIf: you want the safest option. Start here.
strings.channels.latest.name: Latest
strings.channels.latest.serves: The newest release, as soon as it is published. It has not been proven yet.
strings.channels.latest.chooseIf: you want new fixes without waiting.
strings.channels.beta.name: Beta
strings.channels.beta.serves: Built from the official beta versions: what the next release will bring, and the bugs a beta comes with.
strings.channels.beta.chooseIf: you want to test ahead and report what breaks.
strings.channels.note: Most of the time stable and latest hold the same version. They differ after a new release, until it has been proven.

strings.install.rpm.key: Import the signing key once, whichever channel you pick:
strings.downloads.heading: Download a file directly
strings.downloads.intro: For a distribution this repository does not cover, or to install without subscribing to it. Each version links to its release notes, and the checksums of every file follow the table.
strings.downloads.note: Installing a file by hand does not subscribe the machine to updates. Add the repository above for that.
strings.checksums.heading: Checksums
strings.checksums.intro: The SHA-256 checksum of each file, as published with its release. The command under each list checks the files you downloaded: run it in their folder, and it says for each one whether it is the file that was released, OK or FAILED on a system in English, in the language of your system otherwise.
strings.checksums.command: To check them all at once, run this in the folder you downloaded to:
strings.changing.heading: Changing channel later
strings.changing.text: Replace the file you created and update: on Debian and friends /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-desktop.list, on Fedora and friends /etc/yum.repos.d/github-desktop.repo. There is one file and one package name, so a machine follows one channel at a time.
strings.changing.note: Moving down a channel, from beta to stable for instance, means removing the package first: the version you already have is the higher one, and package managers refuse to go backwards on their own.
strings.key.heading: Signing key
strings.key.text: Every index in this repository is signed with that key. Your package manager checks the signature on each update and refuses anything it cannot verify.
strings.footer: Sources, releases and issues: github.com/NitramO-YT/Github-Desktop. This is an unofficial Linux port of GitHub Desktop, not affiliated with GitHub.
